pipesnphysics.ponder.equalizing_fluids.t: The higher the fluid stands, the harder it presses at the bottom
Connected by a pipe, the higher level pushes fluid toward the lower one
The flow slows down as the levels approach each other
and stops once both surfaces stand at the same height
pipesnphysics.ponder.pipe_gravity.text_1: Fluid stored high up wants to come down
pipesnphysics.ponder.pipe_gravity.text_2: Through pipes it flows downhill on its own, no pump needed
pipesnphysics.ponder.pipe_gravity.text_3: It rests at the lowest spot it can reach, until something pushes it
pipesnphysics.ponder.pipe_gravity.text_4: A tank only drains while its fluid stands above the pipe opening
pipesnphysics.ponder.pipe_gravity.text_5: Fluid below the opening stays behind, so connect as low as you can
pipesnphysics.ponder.pipe_overview.text_: Pipes carry fluid between tanks and machines
A Wrench turns a straight pipe into a windowed one, showing the fluid inside
Windowed pipes only run straight through, they cannot branch sideways
A powered pump then drives the fluid through the run
It takes time to travel, filling one pipe after another
Unlike in vanilla Create, each pipe really holds fluid, up to 250 mB
pipesnphysics.ponder.pump_intro.text_1: Fluid sits in a tank until something moves it
pipesnphysics.ponder.pump_intro.text_2: A Mechanical Pump moves it through pipes, out of the side its arrow points
pipesnphysics.ponder.pump_intro.text_3: It only works while rotation powers it
pipesnphysics.ponder.pump_intro.text_4: Watch the fluid travel, filling each pipe on its way
pipesnphysics.ponder.pump_intro.text_5: Faster rotation moves more fluid, but costs more Stress Units
pipesnphysics.ponder.pump_vertically.tex: This tank sits high above the supply
Only the height of the climb matters, not the length of the pipe
Pumps push far better than they pull, so keep them close to the supply
At low speed this pump cannot lift the fluid all the way
A second pump on the same line adds its lift on top
Together they reach the top, faster rotation would as well
pipesnphysics.ponder.siphon.header: Draining over an Obstacle: The Siphon
pipesnphysics.ponder.siphon.text_1: This full tank must drain past the ridge
pipesnphysics.ponder.siphon.text_2: The pipe climbs over the ridge. Its highest point is called the crest
pipesnphysics.ponder.siphon.text_3: Nothing flows yet, because the pipe over the crest is dry
pipesnphysics.ponder.siphon.text_4: Fluid cannot climb into an empty pipe on its own
pipesnphysics.ponder.siphon.text_5: A pump whose lift reaches the crest can fill the line. This is called priming
pipesnphysics.ponder.siphon.text_6: Once primed, the pump is no longer needed
pipesnphysics.ponder.siphon.text_7: This is a siphon. The height difference keeps it flowing on its own
pipesnphysics.ponder.siphon.text_8: It runs until the surfaces level out, or air enters the pipe
pipesnphysics.ponder.tag.fluid_physics.d: How fluids behave in pipes: gravity, equalizing levels, pumping uphill and siphons
pipesnphysics.ponder.valve_throttle.head: Controlling Flow with Valves
pipesnphysics.ponder.valve_throttle.text: A Fluid Valve sits in a pipe run and starts fully open
Turning the handle winds the valve shut, and the flow stops
It holds its position while the handle rests
A valve stopped halfway lets only half the flow through
A Valve Handle turns the valve by a set amount with each use
A dial on its side can restrict the direction, so fluid passes one way only
The far tank now stands higher, but cannot push back through the valve
Allowed both ways again, the higher side drains back
